previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with chronic pancreatitis, type 2 diabetes, and a history of Puestow procedure was admitted for acute-on-chronic abdominal pain lasting three weeks, associated with nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. The pain was described as a deep epigastric ache radiating to the left side and back, different from his usual pattern, and exacerbated by a symptomatic ventral hernia. He reported syncopal episodes with incontinence during severe pain, previously evaluated as likely pseudoseizures. Abdominal imaging showed no obstruction or free air. He was managed with IV fluids, pain control with IV then oral Dilaudid, and temporary dietary restriction. His insulin was adjusted due to hypoglycemia on admission, with Lantus reduced from 10 to 5 units at bedtime. He tolerated advancement to a regular diet, and his symptoms improved. He was discharged home with instructions to continue medications, follow up with his primary care provider, and attend scheduled mental health appointments.

radiology_notes.text:
ABDOMINAL RADIOGRAPH PERFORMED ON ___.

Comparison is made with a prior study from ___ and a CT abdomen and pelvis
from ___.

CLINICAL HISTORY:  Tachycardia and ventral hernia, question SBO.

FINDINGS:  Five images of the abdomen were performed including left lateral
decubitus and upright projections.  The bowel gas pattern is unremarkable
without evidence of ileus or obstruction.  Surgical clips are noted in the
right upper quadrant likely from prior cholecystectomy.  There is no evidence
of free air below the right hemidiaphragm or along the liver edge on the left
lateral decubitus view.  Lung bases appear clear.  Bony structures appear
intact.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of bowel obstruction or free air.

CHEST RADIOGRAPH PERFORMED ON ___

Comparison is made with a prior study from ___.

CLINICAL HISTORY:  Tachycardia, question acute process in the chest.

FINDINGS:  Upright AP view of the chest obtained.  The lungs are clear
bilaterally.  No free air below the right hemidiaphragm.  Cardiomediastinal
silhouette is normal.  Bony structures are intact.

IMPRESSION:  No acute intrathoracic process.  No evidence of pneumoperitoneum.

HISTORY:  Abdominal pain and known hernia but with now diffuse abdominal pain.
The patient is status post Roux-en-Y pancreaticojejunostomy (Puestow
procedure) ___.

COMPARISONS:  Multiple prior CT exams from ___ and
___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT-acquired axial images were obtained through the abdomen and
pelvis with intravenous contrast only.  Coronal and sagittal reformations were
evaluated.

CT OF THE ABDOMEN WITH INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST:  Limited evaluation of lung bases
is unremarkable.  Post-surgical changes from prior Puestow procedure with
Roux-en-Y pancreaticojejunostomy and distal enteroenteric anastomosis are
again seen.  There is new dilatation involving the duodenum and proximal loops
of jejunum, which measure up to 4 cm in size and are fluid filled, but without
a clear transition point.  There does appear to be some tapering of the bowel
in the midline (2:44), with the more distal loops of small bowel appearing
largely decompressed with the exception of the enteroentero anastomotic site
which also appears air filled and slightly dilated, and may relate to the
side-to-side anastomosis.  While there is slight twisting of the mesentery,
this has not significantly changed from prior exams and there is no secondary
mesenteric induration or findings of a closed-loop obstruction.

Remaining intra-abdominal organs including the liver, spleen, pancreas with
diffuse calcifications and mild atrophy consistent with a known history of
pancreatitis, adrenal glands, and kidneys appear unremarkable.  No free air,
free fluid, or pathologically enlarged lymph nodes are identified.  The
patient is status post cholecystectomy.

CT OF THE PELVIS WITH INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST:  Air is noted within the large
bowel and there is reidentification of a transverse colon containing ventral
hernia with a 6-cm neck.  There are no secondary imaging findings of
obstruction or strangulation/incarceration.  Bladder is moderately distended. 
No pathologically enlarged pelvic lymph nodes are seen.

BONE WINDOWS:  No malignant-appearing osseous lesions.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Findings suggestive of mild-to-moderate proximal small-bowel obstruction,
likely partial, with no discrete transition point identified.

2.  Unchanged transverse colon containing ventral hernia with no other
secondary findings of obstruction or strangulation.

3.  Post-surgical changes from prior Puestow procedure with stable appearance
to sequelae of chronic pancreatitis.

NOTE:  Since ___, this patient has had a total of 17 CT abdomen and pelvic
examinations available in our PACS system.  A high index of suspicion for
ordering future CT exams (with preferential use of ultrasound, MRI, or plain
films)  should be used in the future to minimize patients cummulative radation
dose.
